contrast.design: affected vs unaffected regions (difference-in-differences), in-space and in-time placebos, synthetic control

effects.title: Florida grid electricity demand
effects.headline: Florida grid demand, −20% against unaffected regions
effects.plain: Over the seven days from 7 Oct 2024, the two utilities serving most of Florida drew 20% less power than 51 grid regions the storm never touched. On 10 Oct 2024, the day after landfall, the gap was widest: 36% below.

sources.text: 1 source (EIA-930 hourly demand); the second and third channels of the 6.1 test have not run

mechanism.step: Wind and flooding knock out power to millions of customers
mechanism.why: Demand that cannot be served is not recorded as demand.

mechanism.step: Businesses and homes that still have power go dark or empty
mechanism.why: Evacuations and closures cut load even where lines hold.

mechanism.step: Demand climbs back as crews restore lines
mechanism.why: The gap to unaffected regions narrows over the following two weeks in the series.

effects.how: We took the same seven-day window at the same date in every other year of the panel (41 pseudo-storms) and at 30 random sets of two unaffected grid regions. None of the 41 pseudo-storms produced a gap this large; among the 30 random region sets the real Florida pair ranked first, so the in-space p is 1 in 31.
effects.mind: A reporting gap at either utility on those days, or a cold snap that hit Florida but not the donor regions, would make us re-check the size. A flat pre-trend (p 0.42) and a synthetic-control estimate with the same sign both argue against a coincidence of timing.

replication.rule: seen = the pre-registered regional contrast passed (in-space p <= 0.05, pre-trends flat, expected sign)

family.note: Across the 27 past storms tested (24 once overlapping storms are merged) the pooled effect is null; most storms are mapped to whole grid operators (MISO, PJM) where a landfall is a rounding error. Milton and Ian, both mapped to Florida utilities, are the two that pass.

band.note: treated minus donor gap over the 28-day pre-window, mean ± 2 sd, expressed around the donor index

shore.title: New-business applications in hit states
shore.headline: Where hurricanes usually reach: fewer new businesses, four weeks on
shore.plain: Across 23 past hurricanes, applications to start a business in the hit states ran 3.2% below unaffected states over the following four weeks. Nobody pre-registered this for Milton, so Milton itself is untested on it: this is a rule about storms like it, not evidence about this storm.
